question: Which statement best describes map — transform every element?
options: forEach calls your callback for each element but returns undefined — it's for side effects (logging, DOM updates), not for building a value. If you find yourself pushing into an outer array inside forEach, you usually wanted map or filter instead. You also can't break out of forEach.

reduce walks the array carrying an accumulator. Its callback receives (accumulator, currentItem) and returns the next accumulator; the second argument to reduce is the initial value. It's the most general method — sum, count, group, flatten, or even reimplement map and filter with it. Always pass an initial value to handle empty arrays safely.

map returns a NEW array of the same length where each element is the result of running your callback on the original element. It never mutates the source array. Use it whenever you want to convert a list of one shape into a list of another shape (e.g. user objects into names).

filter returns a NEW array containing only the elements for which the callback returns a truthy value. The result can be shorter than the original (or empty). It's the declarative replacement for a loop that pushes matching items into a new array.
explanation: map returns a NEW array of the same length where each element is the result of running your callback on the original element. It never mutates the source array. Use it whenever you want to convert a list of one shape into a list of another shape (e.g. user objects into names).

question: Which statement best describes forEach — run a side effect per element?
options: sort MUTATES the array in place and, with no arguments, sorts elements as STRINGS — so [10, 2, 1] becomes [1, 10, 2].
